description: A human-resources business partner must decide how to resolve a complaint about repeated interruption and exclusion during project meetings, then finalize a restorative process and short-term working safeguards.

shared_context.S1: Leah has raised concerns that Darius repeatedly interrupted her in project meetings and excluded her from decisions connected to her work.
shared_context.S2: Darius denies intending to exclude Leah, and the team has continued working together while the concern is reviewed.
shared_context.S3: Simone has authority to choose the resolution path and put interim working safeguards into effect.
shared_context.S4: As part of the standard case-review process, Simone meets with the people involved and the employee-relations specialist before finalizing the outcome.

PF1.text: Leah has privately documented exactly three meeting incidents, including dates and the decisions that followed; she told a trusted peer about them but has not submitted the account to Simone because she feared the issue would escalate.

PF2.text: Darius is willing to participate in a facilitated resolution, but only if the facilitator is neutral rather than Elena and he receives a separate preparation meeting first; he wants to make a direct apology without arguing about intent.

PF3.text: Elena already promised Darius informally that Jon, the project operations lead, would conduct Darius's weekly check-ins for exactly 30 days so that the check-ins would not feel like disciplinary monitoring; this promise is not in the case file.

PF4.text: Martin confirmed this week that the reported conduct does not meet the threshold requiring a formal investigation on the current record; the applicable resolution procedure instead requires a neutral facilitator, a written no-retaliation notice, and a follow-up check-in exactly 14 days after the resolution meeting, but he has not yet added that guidance to Simone's case notes.

acceptance_conditions: The matter must use a facilitated resolution rather than a formal investigation.
The case record must document exactly three incidents.
The facilitator must be neutral and not Elena.
Darius must receive a separate preparation meeting before the facilitated resolution.
Jon must conduct Darius's weekly check-ins for exactly 30 days.
A written no-retaliation notice must be issued.
The follow-up check-in must occur exactly 14 days after the resolution meeting.

content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] == 'separate_preparation' and c['target'] == 'Darius' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: all(x in credited_facts for x in ['PF1', 'PF2', 'PF3', 'PF4'])

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in credited_facts

decisive_facts.why: Leah's account changes the documented evidence from an unspecified complaint record to exactly three incidents.
Darius's stated participation condition changes the plan to a neutral facilitator and adds a separate preparation meeting.
Elena's prior promise changes the check-in assignment to Jon and fixes its duration at exactly 30 days.
Martin's confirmed procedure changes the route to facilitated resolution and requires the no-retaliation notice plus a follow-up exactly 14 days later.
